title: Doctor Report
description: Output of the environment check at session start. Doctor has two duties (0.2.0 names both): DRIFT detection — declared toolchain vs actual machine — and HEALTH checking — is the environment usable right now (simulators available, paths writable, disk sufficient, aux tools responding). Exit codes: 0 = ok or warn, 2 = drift/fail, 1 = error (doctor itself broke). Drift and failed health checks are halting conditions: the correct downstream action is a harness-update or environment-repair task, never 'proceed and hope'. Warnings are advisories and do not halt.

status.description: ok: all checks passed. warn: no failures, but advisories present (exit 0). drift: at least one fail — version mismatch, missing tool, unusable resource. error: doctor could not complete.

declaration.description: The harness declaration this report verified against. Optional only for harnesses that predate a committed declaration — a report without it can attest health but cannot attest drift, and conformance requires it.

kind.description: tool: version/presence of a declared toolchain entry. resource: discovery of a usable runtime resource (a simulator, a device). path: existence/writability. capacity: a thresholded quantity (disk, memory). file: presence of an expected artifact (e.g. generated secrets).

requirement.description: What was required, in the check's own terms: a version or range for tool checks, a threshold like '>=20GB' for capacity, 'writable' for path.

found.description: What was actually found: a parsed version, a discovered simulator name+runtime, an available capacity. Never include machine-fact VALUES that are personal paths — reports may land in CI logs and issues.
